verses.restored: Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.

familiar.text: Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.

modern.text: Lord, You have been our dwelling place through all generations.

original.text: תְּפִלָּה֮ לְמֹשֶׁ֪ה אִֽישׁ הָאֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים אֲֽדֹנָ֗י מָע֣וֹן אַ֭תָּה הָיִ֥יתָ לָּ֗נוּ בְּדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר

verses.restored: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.

familiar.text: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.

modern.text: Before the mountains were born or You brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting You are God.

original.text: בְּטֶ֤רֶם הָ֘רִ֤ים יֻלָּ֗דוּ וַתְּח֣וֹלֵֽל אֶ֣רֶץ וְתֵבֵ֑ל וּֽמֵעוֹלָ֥ם עַד ע֝וֹלָ֗ם אַתָּ֥ה אֵֽל

verses.restored: Thou turnest man to destruction; and sayest, Return, ye children of men.

familiar.text: Thou turnest man to destruction; and sayest, Return, ye children of men.

modern.text: You return man to dust, saying, “Return, O sons of mortals.”

original.text: תָּשֵׁ֣ב אֱ֭נוֹשׁ עַד דַּכָּ֑א וַ֝תֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וּבוּ בְנֵי אָדָֽם

verses.restored: For a thousand years in thy sight are but as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night.

familiar.text: For a thousand years in thy sight are but as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night.

modern.text: For in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes, or a watch of the night.

original.text: כִּ֤י אֶ֪לֶף שָׁנִ֡ים בְּֽעֵינֶ֗יךָ כְּי֣וֹם אֶ֭תְמוֹל כִּ֣י יַעֲבֹ֑ר וְאַשְׁמוּרָ֥ה בַלָּֽיְלָה

verses.restored: Thou carriest them away as with a flood; they are as a sleep: in the morning they are like grass which groweth up.

familiar.text: Thou carriest them away as with a flood; they are as a sleep: in the morning they are like grass which groweth up.

modern.text: You whisk them away in their sleep; they are like the new grass of the morning—

original.text: זְ֭רַמְתָּם שֵׁנָ֣ה יִהְי֑וּ בַּ֝בֹּ֗קֶר כֶּחָצִ֥יר יַחֲלֹֽף

verses.restored: In the morning it flourisheth, and groweth up; in the evening it is cut down, and withereth.

familiar.text: In the morning it flourisheth, and groweth up; in the evening it is cut down, and withereth.

modern.text: in the morning it springs up new, but by evening it fades and withers.

original.text: בַּ֭בֹּקֶר יָצִ֣יץ וְחָלָ֑ף לָ֝עֶ֗רֶב יְמוֹלֵ֥ל וְיָבֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: For we are consumed by thine anger, and by thy wrath are we troubled.

familiar.text: For we are consumed by thine anger, and by thy wrath are we troubled.

modern.text: For we are consumed by Your anger and terrified by Your wrath.

verses.restored: Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, our secret sins in the light of thy countenance.

familiar.text: Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, our secret sins in the light of thy countenance.

modern.text: You have set our iniquities before You, our secret sins in the light of Your presence.

original.text: שת עֲוֺנֹתֵ֣ינוּ לְנֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ עֲ֝לֻמֵ֗נוּ לִמְא֥וֹר פָּנֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: For all our days are passed away in thy wrath: we spend our years as a tale that is told.

familiar.text: For all our days are passed away in thy wrath: we spend our years as a tale that is told.

modern.text: For all our days decline in Your fury; we finish our years with a sigh.

original.text: כִּ֣י כָל יָ֭מֵינוּ פָּנ֣וּ בְעֶבְרָתֶ֑ךָ כִּלִּ֖ינוּ שָׁנֵ֣ינוּ כְמוֹ הֶֽגֶה

verses.restored: The days of our years are seventy, or eighty if strength endures; yet their span is toil and trouble, for they pass quickly and we fly away.

familiar.text: The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.

notes.title: Seventy or eighty years
notes.body: This poetic observation about human mortality is not a divinely fixed maximum lifespan and should not be treated as a medical or prophetic rule.

modern.text: The length of our days is seventy years— or eighty if we are strong— yet their pride is but labor and sorrow, for they quickly pass, and we fly away.

original.text: יְמֵֽי שְׁנוֹתֵ֨ינוּ בָהֶ֥ם שִׁבְעִ֪ים שָׁנָ֡ה וְאִ֤ם בִּגְבוּרֹ֨ת שְׁמ֘וֹנִ֤ים שָׁנָ֗ה וְ֭רָהְבָּם עָמָ֣ל וָאָ֑וֶן כִּי גָ֥ז חִ֝֗ישׁ וַנָּעֻֽפָה

verses.restored: Who knoweth the power of thine anger? even according to thy fear, so is thy wrath.

familiar.text: Who knoweth the power of thine anger? even according to thy fear, so is thy wrath.

modern.text: Who knows the power of Your anger? Your wrath matches the fear You are due.

original.text: מִֽי י֭וֹדֵעַ עֹ֣ז אַפֶּ֑ךָ וּ֝כְיִרְאָתְךָ֗ עֶבְרָתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Teach us to number our days so that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

familiar.text: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.

modern.text: So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom.

original.text: לִמְנ֣וֹת יָ֭מֵינוּ כֵּ֣ן הוֹדַ֑ע וְ֝נָבִ֗א לְבַ֣ב חָכְמָֽה

verses.restored: Return, O YHWH, how long? and let it repent thee concerning thy servants.

familiar.text: Return, O LORD, how long? and let it repent thee concerning thy servants.

modern.text: Return, O LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants.

original.text: שׁוּבָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה עַד מָתָ֑י וְ֝הִנָּחֵ֗ם עַל עֲבָדֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: O satisfy us early with thy mercy; that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.

familiar.text: O satisfy us early with thy mercy; that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.

modern.text: Satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion, that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.

original.text: שַׂבְּעֵ֣נוּ בַבֹּ֣קֶר חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ וּֽנְרַנְּנָ֥ה וְ֝נִשְׂמְחָ֗ה בְּכָל יָמֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Make us glad according to the days wherein thou hast afflicted us, and the years wherein we have seen evil.

familiar.text: Make us glad according to the days wherein thou hast afflicted us, and the years wherein we have seen evil.

modern.text: Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.

original.text: שַׂ֭מְּחֵנוּ כִּימ֣וֹת עִנִּיתָ֑נוּ שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת רָאִ֥ינוּ רָעָֽה

verses.restored: Let thy work appear to thy servants, and thy glory to their children.

familiar.text: Let thy work appear unto thy servants, and thy glory unto their children.

modern.text: May Your work be shown to Your servants, and Your splendor to their children.

original.text: יֵרָאֶ֣ה אֶל עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ פָעֳלֶ֑ךָ וַ֝הֲדָרְךָ֗ עַל בְּנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: And let the beauty of YHWH our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us; yea, the work of our hands establish thou it.

familiar.text: And let the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us; yea, the work of our hands establish thou it.

modern.text: May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us; establish for us the work of our hands— yes, establish the work of our hands!

original.text: וִיהִ֤י נֹ֤עַם אֲדֹנָ֥י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עָ֫לֵ֥ינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָ֭דֵינוּ כּוֹנְנָ֥ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָ֝דֵ֗ינוּ כּוֹנְנֵֽהוּ

translation_notes: This chapter completes corpus coverage as a ChatGPT-authored draft. KJV is retained as a familiar comparison layer; a separate automated reference pass adds BSB and pointed Hebrew without replacing the restored draft.
safety_note: Mortality language is not a fixed lifespan rule, and suffering must not be reduced to punishment.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Psalms witnesses where extant, and other textual witnesses during the global audit. Preserve poetic parallelism, superscriptions, duplicate/parallel psalms, and significant Hebrew/Greek divergences rather than harmonizing them.
